⚡️
Joint Statement
In Support of the Efforts to Strengthen the United Nations Secretary-General’s Mechanism for Investigation of the Alleged Use of Chemical and Biological Weapons
(New York, October 19, 2026)
✍️
We, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, Burkina Faso, the Central African Republic, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Kyrgyz Republic, the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria, the People’s Republic of China, the Plurinational State of Bolivia, the Republic of Belarus, the Republic of Burundi, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Republic of Mali, the Republic of Nicaragua, the Republic of the Niger, the Republic of Tajikistan,
the Russian Federation,
the State of Eritrea,
reaffirm our dedication to protecting humanity from chemical and biological warfare,
recognize the common interest of all humankind in excluding completely the possibility of the use of chemical, bacteriological (biological) and toxin weapons.
Convinced that such use would be
repugnant to the conscience of humankind,
we are determined to condemn any use of toxic chemicals, biological agents or toxins as weapons by anyone, anywhere, at anytime, and to hold accountable those responsible for any such use.
We underline that the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on Their Destruction (BWC), the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on Their Destruction (CWC) and the Protocol for the Prohibition of the Use in War of Asphyxiating, Poisonous or Other Gases, and of Bacteriological Methods of Warfare (Geneva Protocol) are
essential for international peace and security.
We reaffirm that under all circumstances the use, development, production and stockpiling of chemical, bacteriological (biological) and toxin weapons are
prohibited
under Article I of the BWC and under Article I of the CWC.
We urge all States Parties to the BWC and the CWC as a priority to
fully comply
with all their obligations pursuant to those Conventions and to abide by the understandings agreed by the review conferences of the States Parties to the Conventions. <...>
At the same time we recognize that there have been
developments in the field of science and technology
related to the UNSGM and that the situation relating to the CWC, the BWC and the Geneva Protocol regimes (including new challenges and threats such as chemical and biological terrorism) has changed since the establishment of the UNSGM in 1987 and the endorsement of its technical guidelines and procedures in 1990.
Therefore we are convinced that there is
need for intensifying efforts of the international community
with support of the UN Secretariat to strengthen the expert and technical capabilities of the UNSGM. Particular attention should be paid to the UNSGM guidelines and procedures (document A/44/561), which have not been updated with the exception of their technical appendices (few of their points were revised in 2007) since their endorsement by the UN General Assembly resolution А/45/57С dated December 4, 1990.
We reiterate that according to section G of the above-mentioned UNSGM guidelines and procedures the UN Secretary-General should periodically review with the assistance of his appointed expert consultants,
bearing in mind modifications proposed by Member States, the technical guidelines and procedures
contained in Annex I to the 1989 report of the Secretary-General and revise them as necessary for submission to the General Assembly, upon its request.
👉
In light of the above, we call upon the UN Secretary-General to organize
a review of the current UNSGM guidelines and procedures,
the UN General Assembly document А/44/561 dated October 4, 1989, in which they are set out in accordance with paragraph 103 and by analogy to the update conducted in 2007.

⚡️
Russian MFA Statement on the issuance of a US arrest warrant for Cuba’s historic leader Raul Castro
(October 20, 2026)
*
We categorically reject and strongly condemn
the issuance
by a judge in Miami, United States, of an arrest warrant for Cuba’s historic leader, Army General
Raul Castro
.
The political and legal assessments of the events of February 1996
, for which the Americans hold Raul Castro personally responsible,
are set out in
UN Security Council Resolution 1067 (1996)
, adopted on July 26 of that year.
The resolution
contains no calls for measures to hold any individual personally accountable
. This effectively means that the Council, including the US, agreed that this aspect of the incident was closed.
☝️
Bringing baseless, contrived charges more than 30 years later can only be seen as an act of revenge by Miami’s anti-Cuban lobby
– an attempt to settle scores with
Raul Castro
,
who celebrated his 95th birthday in June
.
We wish to emphasise that
further escalating tensions around the Island of Freedom
, which is already enduring extremely difficult times amid an unprecedented trade, economic, financial and energy blockade,
could destabilise the entire Latin American and Caribbean region
. A social upheaval in Cuba could well trigger a mass exodus of Cuban citizens to neighbouring countries, potentially plunging them into a social crisis.
This court ruling might have been regarded merely as
an expression of the sentiments of a particular group of individuals
, were it not for
the events in Venezuela earlier this year
, when its Leader
was abducted
in violation of all norms and principles of international law
.
🤝
For our part, we reaffirm our unwavering solidarity with the Government of fraternal Cuba
, with which we will continue to strengthen our close ties of friendship, mutual support, assistance and comprehensive cooperation.
We are confident that the indomitable Cuban people and their Leaders
will respond with dignity
to this latest attack by foreign ill-wishers.
We wish Russia’s friend, Comrade
Raul Castro
, sound health and continued courage, bravery and strength of spirit –
qualities that have always distinguished him
.
*Unofficial translation

🇨🇺
#RussiaCuba

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's
answers to media questions
concerning the Netherlands’ extremely unfriendly actions towards Russia
(October 20, 2026)
❓
Question: The Kingdom’s First deputy PM and Minister of Defence, Dilan Yesilgoz-Zegerius,
has stated
that The Hague now regards Moscow as an “enemy”. The Russian Embassy in the Netherlands
has sent a note
requesting clarification as to whether this is the Kingdom’s official position or merely the Minister’s personal view. Has the Embassy received a response, and how would you comment on the situation overall?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
Indeed, following
the remarks
by Dilan Yesilgoz-Zegerius,
the Russian Embassy
sent a note
to the Dutch Foreign Ministry.
No official response has been received so far
. Some members of the Dutch cabinet, however, have already rushed to express their views.
Dutch Foreign Minister
Tom Berendsen
essentially confirmed that the Minister’s remarks
reflect the state’s official position.
Prime Minister
Rob Jetten
offered a more detailed explanation at his weekly press conference. He acknowledged that the remarks made by the Defence Minister, who is also his deputy, during parliamentary debates on the Kingdom’s 2027 budget were
aimed primarily at a domestic audience to justify increased military spending
, while also describing them as a “signal to Moscow”.
☝️
It is telling that, when asked what actions Russia had taken directly against the Netherlands, the Prime Minister was unable to answer.
We have repeatedly spoken about the degradation of Western political elites
. This situation in the Netherlands provides further confirmation. Some Dutch politicians appear to have developed such an unhealthy obsession with Russia that even a mention of our country in the most neutral context leaves them unable to think rationally.
Such behaviour increases the risk of the escalation they themselves have set in motion spiralling out of control.
Let us reiterate
: Russia has repeatedly stated that
it has
no hostile intentions whatsoever towards EU or NATO countries.
At the same time, we have always stressed that,
should a genuine threat to our country arise
,
we will use every means necessary at our disposal to neutralise it
.
***
❓
Question: The Dutch authorities
have denied
Russian female gymnasts visas to compete in the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships, taking place in Rotterdam from October 17 to 25. How do you assess this decision?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
First, the Dutch Embassy in Moscow
refused for a long time to accept visa applications
from our national artistic gymnastics team. Then, having manufactured a last-minute rush,
it finally issued visas – but not to everyone
.
On a contrived pretext, citing the position of unnamed EU allies,
it
denied visas
to Russia’s strongest and most decorated female gymnasts
, who were leading medal contenders.
Resorting to
openly chauvinistic, underhand tactics
deliberately designed to weaken our team is entirely consistent with the Dutch authorities’ current moral standards.
❗️
We urge international sports federations, when selecting host countries for tournaments, to bear in mind that the Netherlands is unable to ensure fair and impartial competition.

🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a joint press conference with Foreign Minister of Iran Abbas Araghchi following bilateral talks
(Tehran, October 19, 2026)
Key points
:
🇷🇺
🇮🇷
#RussiaIran
cooperation continues to develop dynamically
, despite the well-known circumstances. We have a solid foundation for further steady progress:
the updated foundational interstate Treaty
, which entered into force on October 2, 2025, and, for the first time, formally established our relations as
a comprehensive strategic partnership
.
•
Russia demonstrates its commitment to
this fundamental document
through concrete action
. At the UN, we thwarted attempts to justify
the illegal acts of aggression by the US and Israel against Iran
. We acted swiftly to provide the friendly Iranian people with
humanitarian assistance
, delivering much-needed medicines and medical supplies. Food supplies are also delivered regularly.
•
We noted robust growth in bilateral trade
. It
increased
by 21%
in 2025 and by
more than 10%
in the first eight months of 2026. An important supporting factor is
the Free Trade Agreement between Iran and the EAEU
, which entered into force in May 2025. Just five days ago, on October 14,
the Iran-Eurasian Economic Commission Joint Committee
held its second meeting.
•
We reviewed the situation resulting from
the unprovoked US-Israeli aggression against Iran
. I reiterated Russia’s readiness to help find acceptable negotiated solutions to this man-made crisis. We welcomed Tehran’s commitment to using diplomacy to establish lasting peace and stability in the region.
•
We believe it is important to restore the pre-crisis situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz
, including freedom of navigation and guarantees that the aggression will not recur. We appreciate the efforts of international mediators working to help secure such a durable agreement.
•
It is important to resume dialogue on the situation in and around Yemen
. The best course would be to return to
the roadmap developed in Saudi Arabia in 2023
, which was acceptable to both the internationally recognised authorities in Aden and the Ansar Allah movement.
•
I thanked our Iranian friends for their objective position on the Ukrainian crisis
. I briefed them on the latest developments and the efforts underway to ensure that the objectives of
the special military operation
are fulfilled unconditionally, preferably through negotiations.
☝️
However, neither the Kiev regime nor its European “patrons” are clearly ready for such talks.
•
The eradication of traditional Orthodox Christianity
, with its centuries-old roots in Ukraine,
adds a religious dimension to the war unleashed against us
. Western Europe would probably feel more comfortable if Ukrainians’ religious beliefs were guided by the so-called
“liberal thinking”
now being actively imposed across Europe
in opposition to traditional Christian values
dating back centuries, even millennia.
• Some claim that Russia supposedly benefits from the crisis in energy markets. Prices are rising, they say, and we are supposedly
“rubbing our hands”
and filling our coffers to continue financing our
“aggression against Ukraine”
, as it is called in the West.
👉
President Putin has
repeatedly stressed
that we have no interest in price volatility
, with prices swinging up and down.
•
As a responsible state, Russia wants stability, including stable prices
. This is essential for planning our long-term development. The latest budget, currently under consideration, is based on precisely this scenario.
